signature_moves: Aggregator-as-ambient-glass-widget: the whole product face is a chromeless Liquid Glass now-playing HUD, not a windowed library; boldness budget spent entirely on the material, every control kept quiet
Single-chroma discipline: exactly one color moment (Spotify-green source badge) against an otherwise pure white-on-glass field — source identity reads because nothing competes
Per-source badge collapses 'which service?' into a small circle on the album art (Apple Music / Spotify / YouTube unified under one panel)
defects: Contrast Dilution — vibrant-white secondary labels (artist, times) over light translucent glass likely <4.5:1 in bright wallpaper regions; bold title survives on weight, thin secondary text is exposed
Low UI contrast — unfilled progress track (translucent white) vs light glass borderline <3:1; remaining duration hard to gauge
Jakob's-Law anonymity (finding, not defect) — card is close to macOS's own Control Center Now Playing tile; native-ness doubles as lack of distinct identity

Brand mismatch (icon, not UI surface) — app icon is a legacy glossy grayscale play-orb (Web-2.0/iOS-6 skeuomorphism), following neither Big Sur squircle nor Icon Composer conventions; dated face on a current-native glass product

aesthetic.direction: Liquid Glass ambient / system-vibrancy — Organic-soft surface (blurred wallpaper, soft translucency, no hard edges) inheriting Apple's Tahoe material language directly rather than a template default
peers: macOS Control Center Now Playing tile

psychology: Jakob's Law — exploited: mimics the familiar system Now Playing widget for instant comprehension; risk is indistinctness (so conventional it reads as the OS module)
Aesthetic-Usability Effect — glassy polish buys perceived quality/trust on first contact
Von Restorff effect — the single Spotify-green badge and the emphasized center pause glyph are the 'one different things' against a monochrome field
Hick's Law — minimal control set (3 transport + progress) keeps decision load near zero, appropriate for an ambient player
Fitts's Law — transport glyphs generously spaced on a floating panel for easy acquisition
Processing fluency — the white-on-light-glass legibility risk is exactly the 'something feels off' failure mode when secondary text dips under contrast floors
notes: ONLY evidence is an idealized marketing cover composite (player card over a pink/lavender Tahoe floral wallpaper + 'Touch ID or Enter Password' lock-screen backdrop). One surface only — a chromeless floating now-playing HUD; no main window, library, sidebar, toolbar, settings, or service-picker seen, so we learn Liqoria's ambient face only. All px are estimated from a downscaled 964x578 image; trust proportions over absolutes. Lineage native but med-confidence: strong Liquid Glass/SF-Symbols/secondary-label cues, but it's a render, not a captured window, so native canon should treat this cautiously. Mode recorded 'light' (bright wallpaper environment) but the surface uses over-glass VIBRANT WHITE labels — an adaptive/duality treatment, not true light-mode ink. Icon (skeuomorphic glossy grayscale play-orb) contradicts the modern glass UI and should not feed icon canon as current-era. Not enough to promote anything; corpus is at 1 app + kit.
